add.title: Add an account
add.sub: An account is a folder where a CLI keeps its own sign-in. Name it and choose its folder; next you sign in with the CLI's own login.
add.claudeDetail: You sign in with claude auth login.
add.codexDetail: You sign in with codex login.
add.name: Name
add.nameHint: Shown in connections, runs and plan limits, as {{cli}} · {{name}}. Each account of a CLI has its own name.
add.nameHintEmpty: Shown in connections, runs and plan limits. Each account of a CLI has its own name.
add.folderExistingDetail: Where {{program}} is already signed in, such as one you set {{variable}} to. Orchester never deletes a folder it did not create.
add.folderNote: Account folders stay outside every project and repository, so a sign-in is never committed. A new folder starts empty: settings and skills in {{folder}} don't come along.
add.noFolderHere: Orchester has no folder for new accounts on this computer; choose a folder you already use.
add.afterHint: You sign in with {{command}}; Orchester runs it with this folder and checks the result.
add.afterBroughtHint: Orchester checks at once who is signed in to it.

accounts.note: Accounts belong to you on this computer; every project can use them. Each is a folder where the CLI keeps its own sign-in. GitHub keeps using gh's signed-in account for now.

default.name: Default
default.identity: The CLI's own folder · sign in to use it

identity.signedIn: Signed in · the CLI doesn't say who
identity.notSignedIn: Not signed in yet · sign in to use it
identity.unsupported: Default is used for {{cli}} on this Mac
identity.noCli: Nothing to check who is signed in with
identity.unread: The CLI's answer about who is signed in can't be read
identity.folderGone: Its folder is gone · runs on it don't start
identity.waiting: Not signed in yet · waiting for the terminal

details.title: {{cli}} · {{name}}
details.folderHint: Where the CLI keeps this sign-in

actions.signInAgain: Sign in again in a terminal

planLimits.title: Plan limits
planLimits.none: No limits reported yet: {{program}} reports them while a run works on this account, or when you check now.
planLimits.noneCodex: No limits read yet: Orchester reads them from {{program}} on its own once someone is signed in.
planLimits.noteClaude: Claude Code reports limits only while it runs, so they are as of the last run or check on this account. Check now runs the smallest turn Claude Code can, a one-word answer on Haiku, which spends a few tokens of this account's plan; Orchester never checks on its own.
planLimits.noteCodex: Orchester reads Codex's limits on its own, without a turn or tokens: when the app starts, when this account changes, after a reset, and every few minutes while the status bar's plan limits or the Usage page are open.

runsGet.title: What runs on this account get
runsGet.text: Orchester starts {{program}} with {{variable}} set to this folder. The CLI then uses this folder's sign-in, settings, skills and saved sessions; what is in {{defaultFolder}} does not apply.
runsGet.default: Orchester starts {{program}} without setting {{variable}}, so it uses {{folder}}, as {{program}} does when you start it yourself.

accounts.noToken: {{program}} wrote the sign-in into this folder when you signed in. Orchester only runs {{statusCommand}} to read who is signed in; it never reads, shows or copies a token.

state.checking: Asking {{statusCommand}} who is signed in to this folder. What was known stays shown until the answer comes.
state.notSignedIn: {{program}} isn't signed in in {{folder}}. Sign in with the CLI's own login; Orchester checks again when the terminal closes.
state.expired: Was signed in as {{email}}; {{program}} now says it is not logged in. New runs on {{account}} don't start until you sign in again.
state.expiredUnknown: {{program}} now says it is not logged in. New runs on {{account}} don't start until you sign in again.
state.cliMissing: Orchester found no {{program}} on the PATH, so it can't check {{account}} here. A connection with its own program file still checks {{account}} with that program when it is tested.
state.unknown: {{program}} {{version}} answered its status command in a form Orchester doesn't know. Runs on {{account}} still start; if the CLI refuses them, the run says so.
state.folderMissing: {{folder}} no longer exists, so runs on {{account}} don't start. Choose where it is now, or remove the account.
state.same: Signed in as {{email}}, like {{account}}. Both draw on one plan: their limits are shared, and moving runs between them adds nothing.
state.unsupported: On macOS claude keeps its sign-in in the Keychain. Until Orchester has checked that each folder gets its own, Claude Code accounts other than Default are unavailable here.
state.notChecked: Not checked yet. Check again asks {{statusCommand}} who is signed in.

signIn.title: Sign in with {{program}}'s own login
signIn.opened: Orchester opened a terminal window running {{command}} for the {{account}} folder. Finish the sign-in there and in your browser; Orchester checks again when the terminal closes.
signIn.notOpened: Open a terminal running {{command}} for the {{account}} folder, or run the command below in a terminal of your own; then check again.
signIn.waiting: Waiting for the terminal to close · opened {{time}}
signIn.ownTerminal: Or run it in a terminal of your own ({{shell}})
signIn.ownNote: Then press Check again. The variable applies to that terminal only; {{program}} in other windows keeps its own sign-in.
signIn.privacy: Orchester doesn't see what you type in the terminal or the browser. {{program}} writes its sign-in into the {{account}} folder; Orchester then runs {{statusCommand}} to read who is signed in.
signIn.saved: {{account}} is saved. You can also sign in later from its page.
signIn.another: Another account's sign-in terminal is open. Finish that sign-in or close its terminal first.
signIn.signedInBody: Checked {{time}}. Runs on {{account}} use this sign-in until it is signed out.
signIn.signedInFactsBody: {{facts}} · checked {{time}}. Runs on {{account}} use this sign-in until it is signed out.
signIn.next: Next, choose {{account}} as the account of a {{cli}} connection in a project.
signIn.stillOutBody: The terminal closed without a sign-in. Open it again, or run the command in a terminal of your own.
signIn.cliMissingBody: Orchester can't open the sign-in without the {{cli}} CLI. Install it, then check again. The folder is kept.
signIn.sameTitle: Signed in as {{email}}, the same account as {{account}}
signIn.sameBody: Both folders draw on one plan, so their limits are shared and moving runs between them adds nothing. Keep both only for separate settings or skills.

rename.note: Connections, runs and plan limits show the new name at once: they hold the account, not its name. The folder keeps its path.

remove.title: Remove {{account}} from Orchester?
remove.connections: {{count}} connections in {{projects}} use {{account}}. They move to the account you choose; their agent profiles, models and pipelines stay as they are.
remove.connectionsOne: 1 connection in {{projects}} uses {{account}}. It moves to the account you choose; its agent profiles, models and pipelines stay as they are.
remove.connectionsBlocked: {{count}} connections in {{projects}} use {{account}}; you choose where they go once nothing runs on it.
remove.connectionsOneBlocked: 1 connection in {{projects}} uses {{account}}; you choose where it goes once nothing runs on it.
remove.noAccount: No account · it stops starting runs
remove.finished: Finished runs keep showing {{account}}: they ran on it. No run is on {{account}} now.
remove.createdFolder: Orchester created its folder. Move it to the Recycle Bin too, or keep it to add it back later as a folder you already use.
remove.trashWindows: Also move {{folder}} to the Recycle Bin
remove.broughtFolder: Orchester didn't create {{folder}}, so it stays as it is, signed in.
remove.running: Run {{run}} is running on {{account}}. A run keeps its account to the end: its agents' sessions live in {{account}}'s folder.
remove.runningReason: Remove after {{run}} ends, or stop that run first
remove.unreadableReason: {{projects}} can't be read, so a run there may be on this account. Remove it once they open
remove.defaultReason: Default is {{program}}'s own folder, {{folder}}, which every {{program}} you start yourself uses. Orchester can't remove it; to stop runs using it, choose other accounts in your connections.

usedBy.title: Connections
usedBy.empty: No connection uses this account yet. Choose it as a connection's account in a project's Connections.
usedBy.unreadable: {{projects}} could not be read; their connections are not counted.
